    27	}

    31	class Rule:

    36	RULES: tuple[Rule, ...] = (
    37	    Rule("buffer memline member", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)b_ml\b")),
    38	    Rule(
    39	        "memline cached/locked member",
    40	        re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)ml_(?:line_ptr|locked(?:_low|_high|_lineadd)?|stack)\b"),
    41	    ),
    42	    Rule(
    43	        "implicit current-buffer line access",
    44	        re.compile(
    45	            r"\bml_(?:get|get_len|replace|replace_len|append|append_flags|delete|delete_flags)\s*\("
    46	        ),
    47	    ),
    48	    Rule("BUFEMPTY macro", re.compile(r"\bBUFEMPTY\s*\(")),
    49	    Rule(
    50	        "writable line access",
    51	        re.compile(r"\bml_get_buf\s*\([^\n]*,\s*(?:TRUE|true)\s*\)"),
    52	    ),

    71	LINE_ACCESS = re.compile(

    79	VARIABLE_MUTATION = re.compile(

    93	def findings_for_line(line: str, line_number: int) -> list[Finding]:
    94	    findings: list[Finding] = []
    95	    for rule in RULES:

   101	def scan_file(path: Path) -> tuple[list[Finding], list[MutationCandidate]]:
   102	    lines = path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines()
   103	    findings: list[Finding] = []
   104	    accesses: list[tuple[int, str]] = []
   105	
   106	    for line_number, line in enumerate(lines, start=1):
   107	        findings.extend(findings_for_line(line, line_number))
   108	        access = LINE_ACCESS.search(line) or LENGTH_ACCESS.search(line)
   109	        if access:
   110	            accesses.append((line_number, access.group("variable")))
   111	
   112	    mutations: list[MutationCandidate] = []
   113	    for access_line, variable in accesses:
   114	        # This is deliberately a review inventory, not a C parser. Limit the
   115	        # search to the following 80 lines to avoid crossing unrelated code.
   116	        for line_number in range(access_line, min(access_line + 80, len(lines))):
   117	            match = VARIABLE_MUTATION.search(lines[line_number])
   118	            if not match:
   119	                continue
   120	            if (
   121	                match.group("variable")
   122	                and re.search(
   123	                    rf"^\s*[A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*\s+\*\s*"
   124	                    rf"{re.escape(match.group('variable'))}\s*=",
   125	                    lines[line_number],
   126	                )
   127	            ):
   128	                continue
   129	            mutated_variable = (
   130	                match.group("variable")
   131	                or match.group("indexed")
   132	                or match.group("argument")
   133	            )
   134	            if mutated_variable == variable and line_number + 1 != access_line:
   135	                mutations.append(
   136	                    MutationCandidate(
   137	                        access_line, line_number + 1, variable, lines[line_number]
   138	                    )
   139	                )
   140	                break
   141	
   142	    return findings, mutations
   143

   145	def write_report(report_path: Path, source_root: Path, repo_root: Path) -> tuple[int, int]:
   146	    scanned_files = 0
   147	    files_with_findings = 0
   148	    total_findings = 0
   149	    rule_totals: Counter[str] = Counter()
   150	    mutation_totals = 0
   151	
   152	    with report_path.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as report:
   153	        report.write("Vim internal buffer/memline access report\n")
   154	        report.write(f"Source root: {source_root.relative_to(repo_root)}\n")
   155	        report.write("Generated by: tools/check_internal_access.py\n\n")
   156	        report.write("Rules:\n")
   157	        for rule in RULES:
   158	            report.write(f"  - {rule.name}\n")
   159	        report.write("\n")
   160	
   161	        for path in source_files(source_root):
   162	            scanned_files += 1
   163	            findings, mutations = scan_file(path)
   164	            if not findings and not mutations:
   165	                continue
   166	
   167	            files_with_findings += 1
   168	            total_findings += len(findings)
   169	            mutation_totals += len(mutations)
   170	            relative_path = path.relative_to(repo_root)
   171	            report.write(f"{relative_path}\n")
   172	            report.write("=" * len(str(relative_path)) + "\n")
   173	            for finding in findings:
   174	                rule_totals[finding.rule] += 1
   175	                report.write(
   176	                    f"{relative_path}:{finding.line_number}: "
   177	                    f"[{finding.rule}] {finding.text}\n"
   178	                )
   179	
   180	            if mutations:
   181	                report.write("Mutation follow-up candidates:\n")
   182	                for mutation in mutations:
   183	                    report.write(
   184	                        f"{relative_path}:{mutation.mutation_line_number}: "
   185	                        f"{mutation.variable} from line "
   186	                        f"{mutation.access_line_number} is mutated: "
   187	                        f"{mutation.text}\n"
   188	                    )
   189	                report.write("\n")
   190	
   191	            file_totals = Counter(finding.rule for finding in findings)
   192	            report.write(
   193	                f"Stats: {len(findings)} access finding(s); "
   194	                f"{len(mutations)} mutation follow-up candidate(s)"
   195	            )
   196	            for rule in RULES:
   197	                if file_totals[rule.name]:
   198	                    report.write(f"; {rule.name}={file_totals[rule.name]}")
   199	            report.write("\n\n")
   200	
   201	        report.write("Totals\n")
   202	        report.write("======\n")
   203	        report.write(f"Source files scanned: {scanned_files}\n")
   204	        report.write(f"Files with findings: {files_with_findings}\n")
   205	        report.write(f"Total access findings: {total_findings}\n")
   206	        report.write(f"Mutation follow-up candidates: {mutation_totals}\n")
   207	        for rule in RULES:
   208	            report.write(f"{rule.name}: {rule_totals[rule.name]}\n")
   209	
   210	    return scanned_files, total_findings
   211

   213	def main() -> int:
   214	    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(

   216	    )
   217	    parser.add_argument(

   219	        type=Path,
   220	        default=None,

   222	    )
   223	    parser.add_argument(
   224	        "--output",
   225	        type=Path,
   226	        default=None,
   227	        help="report path (default: <root>/internal_access.txt)",
   228	    )
   229	    args = parser.parse_args()
   230	
   231	    repo_root = (args.root or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]).resolve()
   232	    source_root = repo_root / "src"

   234	
   235	    if not source_root.is_dir():

   237	    if report_path.parent != repo_root:

   240	    scanned_files, total_findings = write_report(report_path, source_root, repo_root)

<thinking>
**Considering buffer.c implementation**

I see that buffer.c has many implicit uses that should ideally be migrated. The direct accesses need to be justified as they relate to the memline implementation, but buffer.c isn't memline. It seems like phase 3 isn't complete yet. I could create a checker with `IMPLEMENTATION_FILES = {"src/memline.c", "src/buffer.c"}` and document any exceptions. However, I wonder if this might allow additions in buffer.c without raising concerns.
</thinking>

The remaining inventory confirms Phase 3 cannot honestly claim zero legacy consumers yet: `buffer.c` still owns lifecycle/facade internals, while many editing subsystems still use implicit `ml_get()`. I’ll therefore enforce the boundary for newly added code (with an explicit `memline.c` implementation exception), provide an `--all` audit mode for eventual completion, and keep existing legacy findings visible rather than hiding them.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reject new external dependencies on the memline buffer interface.

By default this checks added lines in the working-tree diff.  Use ``--all``
to audit every source file; that mode reports the legacy accesses that still
need migration.  The memline implementation is the only source file exempt
from the check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


SOURCE_SUFFIXES = {".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".inc", ".pro"}
IMPLEMENTATION_FILES = {"src/memline.c"}
RULES = (
    ("direct b_ml access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)b_ml\b")),
    ("memline line pointer access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)ml_line_ptr\b")),
    (
        "implicit current-buffer text access",
        re.compile(
            r"\bml_(?:get|get_len|replace|replace_len|append|append_flags|delete|delete_flags)\s*\("
        ),
    ),
    ("BUFEMPTY macro", re.compile(r"\bBUFEMPTY\s*\(")),
)


def source_path(path: str) -> bool:
    return path.startswith("src/") and Path(path).suffix.lower() in SOURCE_SUFFIXES


def added_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--unified=0", "--no-color", "--"],
        cwd=repo_root,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    findings: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    path = None
    line_number = 0
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            path = line[6:]
            continue
        if not line.startswith("@@"):
            if path is not None and line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
                findings.append((path, line_number, line[1:]))
                line_number += 1
            continue
        match = re.search(r"\+([0-9]+)(?:,([0-9]+))?", line)
        if match:
            line_number = int(match.group(1))
    return findings


def all_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    source_root = repo_root / "src"
    lines: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    for path in sorted(source_root.rglob("*")):
        relative = path.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
        if not path.is_file() or not source_path(relative):
            continue
        for line_number, text in enumerate(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
        ):
            lines.append((relative, line_number, text))
    return lines


def check(repo_root: Path, audit_all: bool) -> list[str]:
    lines = all_lines(repo_root) if audit_all else added_lines(repo_root)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path, line_number, text in lines:
        if path in IMPLEMENTATION_FILES:
            continue
        for name, pattern in RULES:
            if pattern.search(text):
                errors.append(f"{path}:{line_number}: [{name}] {text}")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Reject new external buffer/memline interface accesses."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="repository root (default: inferred from this script's location)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="audit all source files instead of only added diff lines",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    repo_root = (args.root or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]).resolve()
    errors = check(repo_root, args.all)
    mode = "all source files" if args.all else "added source lines"
    if errors:
        print(f"Buffer interface check failed for {mode}:")
        print("\n".join(errors))
        return 1
    print(f"Buffer interface check passed for {mode}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

# 16 bit DOS version: You need to get a very old version of Vim, for several
# years even the tiny build is too big to fit in DOS memory.
#
# 32 bit DOS version: Support was removed in 7.4.1399.  When syncing to before
# that it probably won't build.
#
# Win32s GUI version: Support was removed in patch 7.4.1364.
#
# OS/2 support was removed in patch 7.4.1008.  If you want to give it a try
# sync to before that and check the old version of this Makefile for
# instructions.

VIMVER	= vim-$(MAJOR).$(MINOR)
VERSION = $(MAJOR)$(MINOR)
VDOT	= $(MAJOR).$(MINOR)
VIMRTDIR = vim$(VERSION)

# How to include Filelist depends on the version of "make" you have.
# If the current choice doesn't work, try the other one.

include Filelist
#.include "Filelist"


# All output is put in the "dist" directory.
dist:
	mkdir dist

# Clean up some files to avoid they are included.
# Copy README files to the top directory.
prepare:
	if test -f lang/LICENSE.nsis.txt; then \
		rm -f lang/LICENSE*.nsis.txt; fi
	for name in $(IN_README_DIR); do \
	  cp READMEdir/"$$name" .; \
	  done

# For the zip files we need to create a file with the comment line
dist/comment:
	mkdir dist/comment

COMMENT_RT = comment/$(VERSION)-rt
COMMENT_W32 = comment/$(VERSION)-bin-w32
COMMENT_GVIM = comment/$(VERSION)-bin-gvim
COMMENT_OLE = comment/$(VERSION)-bin-ole
COMMENT_SRC = comment/$(VERSION)-src
COMMENT_HTML = comment/$(VERSION)-html
COMMENT_FARSI = comment/$(VERSION)-farsi

dist/$(COMMENT_RT): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) runtime files for MS-DOS and MS-Windows" > dist/$(COMMENT_RT)

dist/$(COMMENT_W32): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) binaries for MS-Windows" > dist/$(COMMENT_W32)

dist/$(COMMENT_GVIM): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) GUI binaries for MS-Windows" > dist/$(COMMENT_GVIM)

dist/$(COMMENT_OLE): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) MS-Windows GUI binaries with OLE support" > dist/$(COMMENT_OLE)

dist/$(COMMENT_SRC): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) sources for MS-DOS and MS-Windows" > dist/$(COMMENT_SRC)

dist/$(COMMENT_HTML): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) documentation in HTML" > dist/$(COMMENT_HTML)

dist/$(COMMENT_FARSI): dist/comment
	echo "Vim - Vi IMproved - v$(VDOT) Farsi language files" > dist/$(COMMENT_FARSI)

unixall: dist prepare
	-rm -f dist/$(VIMVER).tar.bz2
	-rm -rf dist/$(VIMRTDIR)
	mkdir dist/$(VIMRTDIR)
	tar cf - \
		$(RT_ALL) \
		$(RT_ALL_BIN) \
		$(RT_UNIX) \
		$(RT_UNIX_DOS_BIN) \
		$(RT_SCRIPTS) \
		$(LANG_GEN) \
		$(LANG_GEN_BIN) \
		$(SRC_ALL) \
		$(SRC_UNIX) \
		$(SRC_DOS_UNIX) \
		$(EXTRA) \
		$(LANG_SRC) \
		| (cd dist/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	-rm $(IN_README_DIR)
# Need to use a "distclean" config.mk file
# Note: this file is not included in the repository to avoid problems, but it's
# OK to put it in the archive.
	cp -f src/config.mk.dist dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/auto/config.mk
# Create an empty config.h file, make dependencies require it
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/auto/config.h
# Make sure configure is newer than config.mk to force it to be generated
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/configure
# Make sure ja.sjis.po is newer than ja.po to avoid it being regenerated.
# Same for cs.cp1250.po, pl.cp1250.po and sk.cp1250.po.
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/ja.sjis.po
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/cs.cp1250.po
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/pl.cp1250.po
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/sk.cp1250.po
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/zh_CN.cp936.po
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/ru.cp1251.po
	touch dist/$(VIMRTDIR)/src/po/uk.cp1251.po
# Create the archive.
	cd dist && tar cf $(VIMVER).tar $(VIMRTDIR)
	bzip2 dist/$(VIMVER).tar

# Amiga runtime - OBSOLETE
amirt: dist prepare
	-rm -f dist/vim$(VERSION)rt.tar.gz
	-rm -rf dist/Vim
	mkdir dist/Vim
	mkdir dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	tar cf - \
		$(ROOT_AMI) \
		$(RT_ALL) \
		$(RT_ALL_BIN) \
		$(RT_SCRIPTS) \
		$(RT_AMI) \
		$(RT_NO_UNIX) \
		$(RT_AMI_DOS) \
		| (cd dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	-rm $(IN_README_DIR)
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/vimdir.info dist/Vim.info
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime.info dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR).info
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime/* dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	rmdir dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime
	cd dist && tar cf vim$(VERSION)rt.tar Vim Vim.info
	gzip -9 dist/vim$(VERSION)rt.tar
	mv dist/vim$(VERSION)rt.tar.gz dist/vim$(VERSION)rt.tgz

# Amiga binaries - OBSOLETE
amibin: dist prepare
	-rm -f dist/vim$(VERSION)bin.tar.gz
	-rm -rf dist/Vim
	mkdir dist/Vim
	mkdir dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	tar cf - \
		$(ROOT_AMI) \
		$(BIN_AMI) \
		Vim \
		Xxd \
		| (cd dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	-rm $(IN_README_DIR)
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/vimdir.info dist/Vim.info
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime.info dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR).info
	cd dist && tar cf vim$(VERSION)bin.tar Vim Vim.info
	gzip -9 dist/vim$(VERSION)bin.tar
	mv dist/vim$(VERSION)bin.tar.gz dist/vim$(VERSION)bin.tgz

# Amiga sources - OBSOLETE
amisrc: dist prepare
	-rm -f dist/vim$(VERSION)src.tar.gz
	-rm -rf dist/Vim
	mkdir dist/Vim
	mkdir dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	tar cf - \
		$(ROOT_AMI) \
		$(SRC_ALL) \
		$(SRC_AMI) \
		$(SRC_AMI_DOS) \
		| (cd dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	-rm $(IN_README_DIR)
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/vimdir.info dist/Vim.info
	mv dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime.info dist/Vim/$(VIMRTDIR).info
	cd dist && tar cf vim$(VERSION)src.tar Vim Vim.info
	gzip -9 dist/vim$(VERSION)src.tar
	mv dist/vim$(VERSION)src.tar.gz dist/vim$(VERSION)src.tgz

# MS-DOS sources
dossrc: dist dist/$(COMMENT_SRC)
	-rm -rf dist/vim$(VERSION)src.zip
	-rm -rf dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	tar cf - \
		$(SRC_ALL) \
		$(SRC_DOS) \
		$(SRC_DOS_BIN) \
		$(SRC_AMI_DOS) \
		$(SRC_DOS_UNIX) \
		lang/LICENSE.*.txt \
		lang/README.*.txt \
		| (cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	mv dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime/* dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	rmdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime
	cd dist && zip -9 -rD -z vim$(VERSION)src.zip vim <$(COMMENT_SRC)

dosrt: dist dist/$(COMMENT_RT) dosrt_files
	-rm -rf dist/vim$(VERSION)rt.zip
	cd dist && zip -9 -rD -z vim$(VERSION)rt.zip vim <$(COMMENT_RT)

# Split in two parts to avoid an "argument list too long" error.
# We no longer convert the files from unix to dos fileformat.
dosrt_files: dist prepare
	-rm -rf dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/lang
	cd src && MAKEMO=yes $(MAKE) languages
	tar cf - \
		$(RT_ALL) \
		| (cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	tar cf - \
		$(RT_SCRIPTS) \
		$(RT_DOS) \
		$(RT_NO_UNIX) \
		$(RT_AMI_DOS) \
		$(LANG_GEN) \
		| (cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	tar cf - \
		$(RT_UNIX_DOS_BIN) \
		$(RT_ALL_BIN) \
		$(RT_DOS_BIN) \
		$(LANG_GEN_BIN) \
		| (cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	-rm $(IN_README_DIR)
	mv dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/lang/ dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/readme/
	mv dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime/* dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	rmdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/runtime
# Add the message translations.  Trick: skip ja.mo/ja.euc-jp.mo and use
# ja.sjis.mo instead.  Same for cs.mo / cs.cp1250.mo, pl.mo / pl.cp1250.mo,
# sk.mo / sk.cp1250.mo, zh_CN.mo / zh_CN.cp936.mo, uk.mo / uk.cp1251.mo and
# ru.mo / ru.cp1251.mo.
	for i in $(LANG_DOS); do \
	      if test "$$i" != "src/po/ja.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/ja.euc-jp.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/pl.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/cs.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/sk.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/zh_CN.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/ru.mo" -a "$$i" != "src/po/uk.mo"; then \
		n=`echo $$i | sed -e "s+src/po/\([-a-zA-Z0-9_]*\(.UTF-8\)*\)\(.sjis\)*\(.cp1250\)*\(.cp1251\)*\(.cp936\)*.mo+\1+"`; \
		mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/lang/$$n; \
		mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/lang/$$n/LC_MESSAGES; \
		cp $$i dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/lang/$$n/LC_MESSAGES/vim.mo; \
	      fi \
	    done
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext32
	cp gettext32/libintl-8.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext32/
	cp gettext32/libiconv-2.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext32/
	cp gettext32/libgcc_s_sjlj-1.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext32/
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext64
	cp gettext64/libintl-8.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext64/
	cp gettext64/libiconv-2.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gettext64/


# Used before uploading.  Don't delete the AAPDIR/sign files!
runtime_unix2dos: dosrt_files
	-rm -rf `find runtime/dos -type f -print | sed -e /AAPDIR/d`
	cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar cf - * \
		| (cd ../../../runtime/dos; tar xf -)

dosbin: prepare dosbin_gvim dosbin_w32 dosbin_ole $(DOSBIN_S)
	-rm $(IN_README_DIR)

# make Win32 gvim
dosbin_gvim: dist dist/$(COMMENT_GVIM)

	tar cf - \

		| (cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	cp gvim.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gvim.exe
	cp teew32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/tee.exe
	cp xxdw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/xxd.exe
	cp vimrun.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/vimrun.exe
	cp installw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/install.exe
	cp uninstallw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/uninstall.exe
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/GvimExt32
	cp gvimext.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/GvimExt32/gvimext.dll
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/GvimExt64
	cp gvimext64.dll dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/GvimExt64/gvimext.dll
	cd dist && zip -9 -rD -z gvim$(VERSION).zip vim <$(COMMENT_GVIM)
	cp gvim.pdb dist/gvim$(VERSION).pdb

# make Win32 console
dosbin_w32: dist dist/$(COMMENT_W32)
	-rm -rf dist/vim$(VERSION)w32.zip
	-rm -rf dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim

	cp vimw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/vim.exe
	cp teew32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/tee.exe
	cp xxdw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/xxd.exe
	cp installw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/install.exe
	cp uninstallw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/uninstall.exe
	cd dist && zip -9 -rD -z vim$(VERSION)w32.zip vim <$(COMMENT_W32)
	cp vimw32.pdb dist/vim$(VERSION)w32.pdb

# make Win32 gvim with OLE
dosbin_ole: dist dist/$(COMMENT_OLE)
	-rm -rf dist/gvim$(VERSION)ole.zip
	-rm -rf dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim
	mkdir dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)
	tar cf - \
		$(BIN_DOS) \
		| (cd dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR); tar xf -)
	cp gvim_ole.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/gvim.exe
	cp teew32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/tee.exe
	cp xxdw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/xxd.exe
	cp vimrun.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/vimrun.exe
	cp installw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/install.exe
	cp uninstallw32.exe dist/vim/$(VIMRTDIR)/uninstall.exe

html: dist dist/$(COMMENT_HTML)

# Buffer interface upgrade

## Goal

Make buffer text access go through a buffer-owned interface instead of reaching
through `buf_T` into its `memline_T` implementation. In practical terms, code
should ask a buffer for a line (conceptually `buf->line(lnum)`) rather than
read `buf->b_ml` or rely on the current buffer through `ml_get()`.

This is an internal C refactoring. It must preserve Vim's existing behavior,
including swap-file handling, undo, text properties, autocommands, recovery,
error messages, and the lifetime rules of returned line pointers.

## Current state

- `buf_T` embeds `memline_T b_ml` in `src/structs.h`.
- `ml_get_buf(buf, lnum, will_change)` and `ml_get_buf_len(buf, lnum)` are
  already the main explicit-buffer read entry points.
- `ml_get()`, `ml_get_len()`, `ml_replace()`, `ml_append()`, and
  `ml_delete()` operate on `curbuf` and therefore encode hidden context.
- Many callers inspect `buf->b_ml.ml_line_count` and
  `buf->b_ml.ml_mfp` directly. `BUFEMPTY()` also combines direct field access
  with an implicit current-buffer line lookup.
- Line pointers returned by `ml_get_*()` are temporary: another line access
  can invalidate the previous pointer. Some callers also request a writable
  line with `will_change = TRUE`.
- The first inventory found roughly 1,279 relevant matches across about 70
  source files when searching for `b_ml`, `ml_get*`, and `BUFEMPTY`; this is a
  baseline, not a promise that every match belongs to this migration.

## Proposed interface

Use names that fit Vim's existing C conventions rather than trying to make C
look like C++. The desired call shape is conceptually `buf->line(lnum)`, but
initially the implementation can be ordinary functions:

```c
char_u *buf_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, int will_change);
colnr_T buf_line_len(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum);
linenr_T buf_line_count(buf_T *buf);
int buf_is_loaded(buf_T *buf);
int buf_is_empty(buf_T *buf);
int buf_append_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, char_u *line,
                    colnr_T len, int flags);
int buf_replace_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, char_u *line,
                     colnr_T len, int has_props, int copy);
int buf_delete_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, int flags);
```

The spelling and exact signatures should be settled in the first
implementation patch. The important properties are:

1. Every operation receives the target buffer explicitly.
2. The interface owns bounds checking, loaded/unloaded behavior, cache
   invalidation, and forwarding to memline.
3. Callers do not need to know that the implementation uses a memfile,
   cached line, locked block, or `memline_T`.
4. Read-only and writable access are visibly different. Prefer separate
   functions if that makes accidental mutation harder.
5. Pointer lifetime and whether a returned line includes text properties are
   documented at the interface boundary.

During the transition, current `ml_*` functions can remain as compatibility
wrappers. New code should not add direct `b_ml` access.

## Migration plan

### Phase 0: establish rules and inventory

- Keep this document as the migration checklist.
- Establish the rule: new code must use the buffer interface for line
  content, line count, loaded state, and empty-buffer checks. Direct `b_ml`
  access is permitted only inside the memline implementation until Phase 3.
- Generate a categorized inventory with searches for:
  - `->b_ml` and `curbuf->b_ml`;
  - `ml_get`, `ml_get_buf`, `ml_get_len`, and related accessors;
  - `ml_append`, `ml_replace`, `ml_delete`, and related mutation calls;
  - direct uses of `ml_line_ptr`, `ml_locked`, and memline flags.
- Classify each use as read, mutation, cache/state management, recovery/swap
  implementation, or test/support code. Do not mechanically replace the
  memline implementation itself.
- Run `python3 tools/check_internal_access.py`. Its report is grouped by source
  file in `internal_access.txt`, includes per-file statistics, and ends with
  totals. Treat its mutation section as a review inventory: it heuristically
  identifies line variables obtained from `ml_get*()` and subsequently written;
  verify each candidate against C control flow before changing it.
- Review `ml_get_buf(..., TRUE)` occurrences separately, since they grant
  writable cached-line access even when the returned pointer is not locally
  captured.
#### Phase 0 status

- [x] Access rules established: new consumers must not add direct `b_ml`
  access or implicit current-buffer line operations.
- [x] Inventory tool created at `tools/check_internal_access.py`.
- [x] Inventory generated at `internal_access.txt`, grouped by source file,
  with per-file statistics and totals.
- [x] Mutation follow-up inventory added for line variables returned by
  `ml_get*()` and subsequently written.
- [x] Baseline `make -j2` completed successfully in `src/`.
- [x] Focused `make test_buffer.res` completed successfully in
  `src/testdir/`.

Baseline inventory totals: 449 source files scanned, 81 files with findings,
1,650 access findings, 11 mutation follow-up candidates, and 10 writable-line
accesses. Phase 0 is complete; the next step is Phase 1, adding the
read-only explicit-buffer façade.

### Phase 1: create the read-only façade

- Add explicit-buffer accessors for line, line length, line count, loaded state,
  and empty state near the existing buffer API.
- Implement them as thin wrappers over the existing memline operations, so
  this phase has no semantic change.
- Add the declarations to the appropriate `.pro` file and regenerate
  prototypes with `make proto` when required by the source change.
- Convert a small, representative group first: display, syntax, search, and
  one integration (Python/Lua/Ruby) caller.
- Add assertions or debug-only checks where useful to catch invalid buffers or
  line numbers at the new boundary.

#### Phase 1 status

- [x] Added explicit-buffer read-only accessors: `buf_line()`,
  `buf_line_len()`, `buf_line_count()`, `buf_is_loaded()`, and
  `buf_is_empty()`.
- [x] Kept the accessors as thin wrappers over existing memline behavior.
- [x] Added declarations to `src/proto/buffer.pro`.
- [x] Migrated representative reads in balloon evaluation, channel output,
  quickfix, Python integration, syntax handling, and search.
- [ ] Add dedicated API tests and debug assertions for invalid buffers and
  line numbers.
- [x] Regenerate prototypes with `make proto` after installing the required
  Python `clang.cindex` dependency; only `src/proto/buffer.pro` changed.

The source build and focused buffer test pass with the façade and migrations.
Phase 1 remains open until its API checks and debug assertions are added.

### Phase 2: migrate all consumers

#### Phase 2 progress

- [x] Migrated explicit-buffer `ml_get_buf()` and `ml_get_buf_len()` reads
  outside `memline.c` and the façade implementation to `buf_line()` and
  `buf_line_len()` across 42 source files.
- [x] Regenerated the internal-access inventory after the migration.
- [x] Rebuilt Vim and reran `test_buffer.res` successfully.
- [x] Replace direct line-count field reads and `BUFEMPTY()` uses with
  `buf_line_count()` and `buf_is_empty()` in consumer code.
- [x] Replace loaded-state null checks with `buf_is_loaded()` in consumer
  code, preserving inverse checks and compound conditions.
- [ ] Migrate implicit-current-buffer reads.
- [x] Added buffer-owned mutation APIs: `buf_append_line()`,
  `buf_replace_line()`, and `buf_delete_line()`.
- [x] Migrated mutation consumers, including language integrations and
  `if_py_both.h`, away from `ml_append()`, `ml_replace()`, and `ml_delete()`.
- [x] Added `tools/check_internal_mutations.py` and generated
  `internal_mutations.txt` as the mutation inventory.

The access inventory reports 1,075 findings, including 514 direct `b_ml`
accesses, 460 implicit-current-buffer line accesses, and one writable line
access. The mutation inventory reports 186 findings after the consumer
migration: 44 implicit mutation references, 17 explicit/internal mutation
references, one writable line access, 124 direct memline state mutations, and
two line-pointer follow-up candidates. Remaining mutation findings are
primarily implementation-side operations in `memline.c` and direct cache/state
management that still require deliberate review.

Phase 3 enforcement currently checks only newly added lines, so it does not
hide these pre-existing findings. Run `make check-buffer-interface` for the
presubmit check or `python3 tools/check_buffer_interface.py --all` for the full
audit. `src/memline.c` is the sole implementation exception; `src/buffer.c`
continues to contain legacy buffer lifecycle/facade access that must be
migrated before the boundary can be considered complete.

- Convert reads before mutations, grouping changes by subsystem to keep each
  patch buildable.
- Replace line-count and loaded-state field reads with accessors.
- Replace `BUFEMPTY()` with an explicit-buffer operation; retain a current-
buffer convenience wrapper only where the caller truly means `curbuf`.
- [x] Convert consumer mutation calls to buffer-owned API operations. The
  façade carries the target `buf_T *`; replace/delete compatibility entry
  points still rely on current-buffer context inside the memline implementation
  and return `FAIL` for a non-current buffer until that layer is refactored.
- Continue migrating implicit-current-buffer reads and remove the remaining
  memline context dependency from mutation implementations.
- Update language integrations and any code in headers/macros, not just `.c`
  files. Pay special attention to `if_py_both.h`, where buffer access is
  exposed through several collection operations.
- Leave memline internals (`memline.c` and its private helpers) allowed to use
  `memline_T`; the goal is to stop unrelated subsystems from depending on it.

### Phase 3: enforce the boundary

- Make `memline_T` private to the memline implementation if the include/layout
  structure permits it. If a complete `buf_T` definition must remain public,
  at least remove external direct access to `b_ml` and document the remaining
  implementation-only exceptions.
- Rename or relocate compatibility wrappers once all callers have migrated.
- [x] Add `tools/check_buffer_interface.py`, a presubmit check that rejects
  new external `->b_ml`, `ml_line_ptr`, `BUFEMPTY()`, and implicit
  current-buffer text access.  It checks added source lines by default and
  provides `--all` for auditing the remaining legacy accesses.  The only
  implementation exception is `src/memline.c`.
- [ ] Re-run the inventory and require zero unclassified consumer accesses.

### Phase 4: harden and optimize

- Run the full test suite and feature-matrix builds, including minimal builds
  and language interfaces where available.
- Compare performance of hot paths such as screen drawing, insert/delete,
  syntax, and writing files. Avoid introducing allocations or buffer switches
  merely to obtain a line.
- Consider a future opaque buffer representation only after the accessor
  boundary is complete and measurable.

## Main challenges and decisions

### 1. `buf_T` is not currently opaque

The structure is defined in `src/structs.h` and many subsystems use fields
other than text. Hiding only `b_ml` may require include-order changes and
accessors for related state. Hiding the entire structure is a larger project;
do not couple it to the first line-access migration.

### 2. Implicit `curbuf` is deeply embedded

The existing mutation and convenience APIs often operate on `curbuf`. A
wrapper that silently switches buffers would be fragile: switching can run
autocommands, change windows, invalidate pointers, and alter error context.
The target API must carry `buf_T *` explicitly through the call chain.

### 3. Cached line pointer lifetime

A line pointer is valid only until a subsequent line access can flush or replace
the cache. The interface must preserve this contract or introduce an explicit
copy/borrow type. Do not “improve” lifetime accidentally by allocating every
line; that would affect hot paths and ownership assumptions.

### 4. Writable access and mutation bookkeeping

`ml_get_buf(..., TRUE)` marks cached state for modification, while
`ml_replace()` and friends handle undo, text properties, NetBeans, changed
state, and display updates through surrounding code. Reads and writes need
separate review and tests; a generic `line()` accessor must not make writes
look like harmless reads.

### 5. Unloaded, empty, invalid, and special buffers

A buffer can be never loaded, unloaded, empty, quickfix, terminal, prompt, or
otherwise special. Existing APIs return an empty string, an error marker, or
emit an error depending on the operation. The new interface must specify each
case and preserve the existing result and diagnostics.

### 6. Swap files, recovery, and memline cache state

`memline.c` manages block locking, translation, flushing, encryption, and
recovery. Direct field users may be coupled to these details in subtle ways.
Keep implementation-only operations in memline until their callers have a
well-defined replacement; do not replace state checks with a simplistic
“line count > 0” test.

### 7. Pointer invalidation across callbacks

Autocommands, scripting callbacks, redraw, and NetBeans can run while work is
in progress and may delete or unload a buffer. Existing `bufref_T` patterns
must remain in place. Accessors should not retain raw pointers across calls
that can invoke callbacks without revalidating the buffer.

### 8. Portability and generated declarations

Vim supports old and diverse C compilers. Keep signatures compatible with the
project's C dialect and use Vim types/wrappers. Changes to source functions
may require generated prototype updates; do not hand-edit generated files
unless the repository's normal generation step requires it.

### 9. Performance-sensitive call sites

Screen rendering, cursor movement, insert mode, syntax, and file writing can
access lines in tight loops. Thin inline wrappers may be appropriate after
correctness is established, but first measure rather than expose internals for
speed.

## Validation and completion criteria

A phase is complete only when:

- the relevant build succeeds without new warnings;
- focused buffer, editing, undo, recovery, swap-file, display, and scripting
  tests pass;
- behavior for unloaded and special buffers is covered;
- no newly migrated caller relies on a stale line pointer;
- the inventory is updated and the remaining direct accesses are explicitly
  justified as memline implementation code; and
- the full migration has a reviewable diff, not a broad formatting rewrite.

The overall upgrade is complete when external buffer consumers no longer read
`b_ml` or call implicit-current-buffer line operations, and the memline layout
can be changed without changing those consumers' code.

## Suggested patch sequence

1. Define the accessor contract and add read-only explicit-buffer wrappers.
2. Migrate line reads in one subsystem at a time, starting with low-risk
   consumers and including regression tests.
3. Migrate line count, loaded, and empty checks.
4. Add and migrate explicit-buffer mutation APIs.
5. Migrate integrations and macros; audit callback and `bufref_T` lifetimes.
6. Restrict direct memline access to implementation code and add enforcement.
7. Run full validation and measure hot paths before considering further
   encapsulation.

```
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reject new external dependencies on the memline buffer interface.

By default this checks added lines in the working-tree diff.  Use ``--all``
to audit every source file; that mode reports the legacy accesses that still
need migration.  The memline implementation is the only source file exempt
from the check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path


SOURCE_SUFFIXES = {".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".inc", ".pro"}
IMPLEMENTATION_FILES = {"src/memline.c"}
RULES = (
    ("direct b_ml access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)b_ml\b")),
    ("memline line pointer access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)ml_line_ptr\b")),
    (
        "implicit current-buffer text access",
        re.compile(
            r"\bml_(?:get|get_len|replace|replace_len|append|append_flags|delete|delete_flags)\s*\("
        ),
    ),
    ("BUFEMPTY macro", re.compile(r"\bBUFEMPTY\s*\(")),
)


def source_path(path: str) -> bool:
    return path.startswith("src/") and Path(path).suffix.lower() in SOURCE_SUFFIXES


def added_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--unified=0", "--no-color", "--"],
        cwd=repo_root,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    findings: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    path = None
    line_number = 0
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            path = line[6:]
            continue
        if not line.startswith("@@"):
            if path is not None and line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
                findings.append((path, line_number, line[1:]))
                line_number += 1
            continue
        match = re.search(r"\+([0-9]+)(?:,([0-9]+))?", line)
        if match:
            line_number = int(match.group(1))
    return findings


def all_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    source_root = repo_root / "src"
    lines: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    for path in sorted(source_root.rglob("*")):
        relative = path.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
        if not path.is_file() or not source_path(relative):
            continue
        for line_number, text in enumerate(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
        ):
            lines.append((relative, line_number, text))
    return lines


def check(repo_root: Path, audit_all: bool) -> list[str]:
    lines = all_lines(repo_root) if audit_all else added_lines(repo_root)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path, line_number, text in lines:
        if not source_path(path) or path in IMPLEMENTATION_FILES:
            continue
        for name, pattern in RULES:
            if pattern.search(text):
                errors.append(f"{path}:{line_number}: [{name}] {text}")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Reject new external buffer/memline interface accesses."
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="repository root (default: inferred from this script's location)",
    )
    parser.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="audit all source files instead of only added diff lines",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    repo_root = (args.root or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]).resolve()
    errors = check(repo_root, args.all)
    mode = "all source files" if args.all else "added source lines"
    if errors:
        print(f"Buffer interface check failed for {mode}:")
        print("\n".join(errors))
        return 1
    print(f"Buffer interface check passed for {mode}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reject new external dependencies on the memline buffer interface.

By default this checks added lines in the working-tree diff.  Use ``--all``
to audit every source file; that mode reports the legacy accesses that still
need migration.  The memline implementation is the only source file exempt
from the check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
from pathlib import Path
import re
import subprocess
from typing import cast


SOURCE_SUFFIXES = {".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".inc", ".pro"}
IMPLEMENTATION_FILES = {"src/memline.c"}
RULES = (
    ("direct b_ml access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)b_ml\b")),
    ("memline line pointer access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)ml_line_ptr\b")),
    (
        "implicit current-buffer text access",
        re.compile(
            r"\bml_(?:get|get_len|replace|replace_len|append|append_flags|delete|delete_flags)\s*\("
        ),
    ),
    ("BUFEMPTY macro", re.compile(r"\bBUFEMPTY\s*\(")),
)


def source_path(path: str) -> bool:
    return path.startswith("src/") and Path(path).suffix.lower() in SOURCE_SUFFIXES


def added_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "--no-ext-diff", "--unified=0", "--no-color", "--"],
        cwd=repo_root,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    findings: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    path = None
    line_number = 0
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            path = line[6:]
            continue
        if not line.startswith("@@"):
            if path is not None and line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
                findings.append((path, line_number, line[1:]))
                line_number += 1
            continue
        match = re.search(r"\+([0-9]+)(?:,([0-9]+))?", line)
        if match:
            line_number = int(match.group(1))
    return findings


def all_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    source_root = repo_root / "src"
    lines: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    for path in sorted(source_root.rglob("*")):
        relative = path.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
        if not path.is_file() or not source_path(relative):
            continue
        for line_number, text in enumerate(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
        ):
            lines.append((relative, line_number, text))
    return lines


def check(repo_root: Path, audit_all: bool) -> list[str]:
    lines = all_lines(repo_root) if audit_all else added_lines(repo_root)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path, line_number, text in lines:
        if not source_path(path) or path in IMPLEMENTATION_FILES:
            continue
        for name, pattern in RULES:
            if pattern.search(text):
                errors.append(f"{path}:{line_number}: [{name}] {text}")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Reject new external buffer/memline interface accesses."
    )
    _ = parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="repository root (default: inferred from this script's location)",
    )
    _ = parser.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="audit all source files instead of only added diff lines",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root_arg = cast(Path | None, args.root)
    audit_all = cast(bool, args.all)
    repo_root = (root_arg or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]).resolve()
    errors = check(repo_root, audit_all)
    mode = "all source files" if audit_all else "added source lines"
    if errors:
        print(f"Buffer interface check failed for {mode}:")
        print("\n".join(errors))
        return 1
    print(f"Buffer interface check passed for {mode}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

        relative = path.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
        if not path.is_file() or not source_path(relative):
            continue
        for line_number, text in enumerate(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
        ):
            lines.append((relative, line_number, text))
    return lines


def check(repo_root: Path, audit_all: bool) -> list[str]:
    lines = all_lines(repo_root) if audit_all else added_lines(repo_root)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path, line_number, text in lines:
        if not source_path(path) or path in IMPLEMENTATION_FILES:
            continue
        for name, pattern in RULES:
            if pattern.search(text):
                errors.append(f"{path}:{line_number}: [{name}] {text}")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Reject new external buffer/memline interface accesses."
    )
    _ = parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="repository root (default: inferred from this script's location)",
    )
    _ = parser.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="audit all source files instead of only added diff lines",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root_arg = cast(Path | None, args.root)
    audit_all = cast(bool, args.all)
    repo_root = (root_arg or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]).resolve()
    errors = check(repo_root, audit_all)
    mode = "all source files" if audit_all else "added source lines"
    if errors:
        print(f"Buffer interface check failed for {mode}:")
        print("\n".join(errors))
        return 1
    print(f"Buffer interface check passed for {mode}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Reject new external dependencies on the memline buffer interface.

By default this checks added lines relative to ``HEAD`` and untracked source
files.  Use ``--all`` to audit every source file; that mode reports the legacy
accesses that still
need migration.  The memline implementation is the only source file exempt
from the check.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import re
import subprocess
from pathlib import Path
from typing import cast

SOURCE_SUFFIXES = {".c", ".cc", ".cpp", ".h", ".inc", ".pro"}
IMPLEMENTATION_FILES = {"src/memline.c"}
RULES = (
    ("direct b_ml access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)b_ml\b")),
    ("memline line pointer access", re.compile(r"(?:->|\.)ml_line_ptr\b")),
    (
        "implicit current-buffer text access",
        re.compile(
            r"\bml_(?:get|get_len|replace|replace_len|append|append_flags|delete|delete_flags)\s*\("
        ),
    ),
    ("BUFEMPTY macro", re.compile(r"\bBUFEMPTY\s*\(")),
)


def source_path(path: str) -> bool:
    return path.startswith("src/") and Path(path).suffix.lower() in SOURCE_SUFFIXES


def added_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "diff", "HEAD", "--no-ext-diff", "--unified=0", "--no-color", "--"],
        cwd=repo_root,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    findings: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    path = None
    line_number = 0
    for line in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith("+++ b/"):
            path = line[6:]
            continue
        if not line.startswith("@@"):
            if path is not None and line.startswith("+") and not line.startswith("+++"):
                findings.append((path, line_number, line[1:]))
                line_number += 1
            continue
        match = re.search(r"\+([0-9]+)(?:,([0-9]+))?", line)
        if match:
            line_number = int(match.group(1))
    return findings


def untracked_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    result = subprocess.run(
        ["git", "ls-files", "--others", "--exclude-standard", "--", "src/"],
        cwd=repo_root,
        check=True,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
    )
    lines: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    for relative in result.stdout.splitlines():
        if not source_path(relative):
            continue
        path = repo_root / relative
        for line_number, text in enumerate(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
        ):
            lines.append((relative, line_number, text))
    return lines


def all_lines(repo_root: Path) -> list[tuple[str, int, str]]:
    source_root = repo_root / "src"
    lines: list[tuple[str, int, str]] = []
    for path in sorted(source_root.rglob("*")):
        relative = path.relative_to(repo_root).as_posix()
        if not path.is_file() or not source_path(relative):
            continue
        for line_number, text in enumerate(
            path.read_text(encoding="utf-8", errors="replace").splitlines(), 1
        ):
            lines.append((relative, line_number, text))
    return lines


def check(repo_root: Path, audit_all: bool) -> list[str]:
    lines = all_lines(repo_root) if audit_all else added_lines(repo_root) + untracked_lines(repo_root)
    errors: list[str] = []
    for path, line_number, text in lines:
        if not source_path(path) or path in IMPLEMENTATION_FILES:
            continue
        for name, pattern in RULES:
            if pattern.search(text):
                errors.append(f"{path}:{line_number}: [{name}] {text}")
    return errors


def main() -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        description="Reject new external buffer/memline interface accesses."
    )
    _ = parser.add_argument(
        "--root",
        type=Path,
        default=None,
        help="repository root (default: inferred from this script's location)",
    )
    _ = parser.add_argument(
        "--all",
        action="store_true",
        help="audit all source files instead of only added diff lines",
    )
    args = parser.parse_args()
    root_arg = cast(Path | None, args.root)
    audit_all = cast(bool, args.all)
    repo_root = (root_arg or Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]).resolve()
    errors = check(repo_root, audit_all)
    mode = "all source files" if audit_all else "added source lines"
    if errors:
        print(f"Buffer interface check failed for {mode}:")
        print("\n".join(errors))
        return 1
    print(f"Buffer interface check passed for {mode}.")
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

```

# Buffer interface upgrade

## Goal

Make buffer text access go through a buffer-owned interface instead of reaching
through `buf_T` into its `memline_T` implementation. In practical terms, code
should ask a buffer for a line (conceptually `buf->line(lnum)`) rather than
read `buf->b_ml` or rely on the current buffer through `ml_get()`.

This is an internal C refactoring. It must preserve Vim's existing behavior,
including swap-file handling, undo, text properties, autocommands, recovery,
error messages, and the lifetime rules of returned line pointers.

## Current state

- `buf_T` embeds `memline_T b_ml` in `src/structs.h`.
- `ml_get_buf(buf, lnum, will_change)` and `ml_get_buf_len(buf, lnum)` are
  already the main explicit-buffer read entry points.
- `ml_get()`, `ml_get_len()`, `ml_replace()`, `ml_append()`, and
  `ml_delete()` operate on `curbuf` and therefore encode hidden context.
- Many callers inspect `buf->b_ml.ml_line_count` and
  `buf->b_ml.ml_mfp` directly. `BUFEMPTY()` also combines direct field access
  with an implicit current-buffer line lookup.
- Line pointers returned by `ml_get_*()` are temporary: another line access
  can invalidate the previous pointer. Some callers also request a writable
  line with `will_change = TRUE`.
- The first inventory found roughly 1,279 relevant matches across about 70
  source files when searching for `b_ml`, `ml_get*`, and `BUFEMPTY`; this is a
  baseline, not a promise that every match belongs to this migration.

## Proposed interface

Use names that fit Vim's existing C conventions rather than trying to make C
look like C++. The desired call shape is conceptually `buf->line(lnum)`, but
initially the implementation can be ordinary functions:

```c
char_u *buf_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, int will_change);
colnr_T buf_line_len(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum);
linenr_T buf_line_count(buf_T *buf);
int buf_is_loaded(buf_T *buf);
int buf_is_empty(buf_T *buf);
int buf_append_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, char_u *line,
                    colnr_T len, int flags);
int buf_replace_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, char_u *line,
                     colnr_T len, int has_props, int copy);
int buf_delete_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, int flags);
```

The spelling and exact signatures should be settled in the first
implementation patch. The important properties are:

1. Every operation receives the target buffer explicitly.
2. The interface owns bounds checking, loaded/unloaded behavior, cache
   invalidation, and forwarding to memline.
3. Callers do not need to know that the implementation uses a memfile,
   cached line, locked block, or `memline_T`.
4. Read-only and writable access are visibly different. Prefer separate
   functions if that makes accidental mutation harder.
5. Pointer lifetime and whether a returned line includes text properties are
   documented at the interface boundary.

During the transition, current `ml_*` functions can remain as compatibility
wrappers. New code should not add direct `b_ml` access.

## Migration plan

### Phase 0: establish rules and inventory

- Keep this document as the migration checklist.
- Establish the rule: new code must use the buffer interface for line
  content, line count, loaded state, and empty-buffer checks. Direct `b_ml`
  access is permitted only inside the memline implementation until Phase 3.
- Generate a categorized inventory with searches for:
  - `->b_ml` and `curbuf->b_ml`;
  - `ml_get`, `ml_get_buf`, `ml_get_len`, and related accessors;
  - `ml_append`, `ml_replace`, `ml_delete`, and related mutation calls;
  - direct uses of `ml_line_ptr`, `ml_locked`, and memline flags.
- Classify each use as read, mutation, cache/state management, recovery/swap
  implementation, or test/support code. Do not mechanically replace the
  memline implementation itself.
- Run `python3 tools/check_internal_access.py`. Its report is grouped by source
  file in `internal_access.txt`, includes per-file statistics, and ends with
  totals. Treat its mutation section as a review inventory: it heuristically
  identifies line variables obtained from `ml_get*()` and subsequently written;
  verify each candidate against C control flow before changing it.
- Review `ml_get_buf(..., TRUE)` occurrences separately, since they grant
  writable cached-line access even when the returned pointer is not locally
  captured.

### Phase 3: enforce the boundary

- Make `memline_T` private to the memline implementation if the include/layout
  structure permits it. If a complete `buf_T` definition must remain public,

  provides `--all` for auditing the remaining legacy accesses.  The only

- [ ] Re-run the inventory and require zero unclassified consumer accesses.

- Run the full test suite and feature-matrix builds, including minimal builds

- Compare performance of hot paths such as screen drawing, insert/delete,

- Consider a future opaque buffer representation only after the accessor
  boundary is complete and measurable.

## Main challenges and decisions

### 1. `buf_T` is not currently opaque

The structure is defined in `src/structs.h` and many subsystems use fields
other than text. Hiding only `b_ml` may require include-order changes and
accessors for related state. Hiding the entire structure is a larger project;
do not couple it to the first line-access migration.

### 2. Implicit `curbuf` is deeply embedded

The existing mutation and convenience APIs often operate on `curbuf`. A
wrapper that silently switches buffers would be fragile: switching can run
autocommands, change windows, invalidate pointers, and alter error context.
The target API must carry `buf_T *` explicitly through the call chain.

### 3. Cached line pointer lifetime

A line pointer is valid only until a subsequent line access can flush or replace
the cache. The interface must preserve this contract or introduce an explicit
copy/borrow type. Do not “improve” lifetime accidentally by allocating every
line; that would affect hot paths and ownership assumptions.

### 4. Writable access and mutation bookkeeping

`ml_get_buf(..., TRUE)` marks cached state for modification, while
`ml_replace()` and friends handle undo, text properties, NetBeans, changed
state, and display updates through surrounding code. Reads and writes need
separate review and tests; a generic `line()` accessor must not make writes
look like harmless reads.

### 5. Unloaded, empty, invalid, and special buffers

A buffer can be never loaded, unloaded, empty, quickfix, terminal, prompt, or
otherwise special. Existing APIs return an empty string, an error marker, or
emit an error depending on the operation. The new interface must specify each
case and preserve the existing result and diagnostics.

### 6. Swap files, recovery, and memline cache state

`memline.c` manages block locking, translation, flushing, encryption, and
recovery. Direct field users may be coupled to these details in subtle ways.
Keep implementation-only operations in memline until their callers have a
well-defined replacement; do not replace state checks with a simplistic
“line count > 0” test.

### 7. Pointer invalidation across callbacks

Autocommands, scripting callbacks, redraw, and NetBeans can run while work is
in progress and may delete or unload a buffer. Existing `bufref_T` patterns
must remain in place. Accessors should not retain raw pointers across calls
that can invoke callbacks without revalidating the buffer.

### 8. Portability and generated declarations

Vim supports old and diverse C compilers. Keep signatures compatible with the
project's C dialect and use Vim types/wrappers. Changes to source functions
may require generated prototype updates; do not hand-edit generated files
unless the repository's normal generation step requires it.

### 9. Performance-sensitive call sites

Screen rendering, cursor movement, insert mode, syntax, and file writing can
access lines in tight loops. Thin inline wrappers may be appropriate after
correctness is established, but first measure rather than expose internals for
speed.

## Validation and completion criteria

A phase is complete only when:

- the relevant build succeeds without new warnings;
- focused buffer, editing, undo, recovery, swap-file, display, and scripting
  tests pass;
- behavior for unloaded and special buffers is covered;
- no newly migrated caller relies on a stale line pointer;
- the inventory is updated and the remaining direct accesses are explicitly
  justified as memline implementation code; and
- the full migration has a reviewable diff, not a broad formatting rewrite.

The overall upgrade is complete when external buffer consumers no longer read
`b_ml` or call implicit-current-buffer line operations, and the memline layout
can be changed without changing those consumers' code.

## Suggested patch sequence

1. Define the accessor contract and add read-only explicit-buffer wrappers.
2. Migrate line reads in one subsystem at a time, starting with low-risk
   consumers and including regression tests.
3. Migrate line count, loaded, and empty checks.
4. Add and migrate explicit-buffer mutation APIs.
5. Migrate integrations and macros; audit callback and `bufref_T` lifetimes.
6. Restrict direct memline access to implementation code and add enforcement.
7. Run full validation and measure hot paths before considering further
   encapsulation.

# Buffer interface upgrade

## Goal

Make buffer text access go through a buffer-owned interface instead of reaching
through `buf_T` into its `memline_T` implementation. In practical terms, code
should ask a buffer for a line (conceptually `buf->line(lnum)`) rather than
read `buf->b_ml` or rely on the current buffer through `ml_get()`.

This is an internal C refactoring. It must preserve Vim's existing behavior,
including swap-file handling, undo, text properties, autocommands, recovery,
error messages, and the lifetime rules of returned line pointers.

## Current state

- `buf_T` embeds `memline_T b_ml` in `src/structs.h`.
- `ml_get_buf(buf, lnum, will_change)` and `ml_get_buf_len(buf, lnum)` are
  already the main explicit-buffer read entry points.
- `ml_get()`, `ml_get_len()`, `ml_replace()`, `ml_append()`, and
  `ml_delete()` operate on `curbuf` and therefore encode hidden context.
- Many callers inspect `buf->b_ml.ml_line_count` and
  `buf->b_ml.ml_mfp` directly. `BUFEMPTY()` also combines direct field access
  with an implicit current-buffer line lookup.
- Line pointers returned by `ml_get_*()` are temporary: another line access
  can invalidate the previous pointer. Some callers also request a writable
  line with `will_change = TRUE`.
- The first inventory found roughly 1,279 relevant matches across about 70
  source files when searching for `b_ml`, `ml_get*`, and `BUFEMPTY`; this is a
  baseline, not a promise that every match belongs to this migration.

## Proposed interface

Use names that fit Vim's existing C conventions rather than trying to make C
look like C++. The desired call shape is conceptually `buf->line(lnum)`, but
initially the implementation can be ordinary functions:

```c
char_u *buf_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, int will_change);
colnr_T buf_line_len(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum);
linenr_T buf_line_count(buf_T *buf);
int buf_is_loaded(buf_T *buf);
int buf_is_empty(buf_T *buf);
int buf_append_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, char_u *line,
                    colnr_T len, int flags);
int buf_replace_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, char_u *line,
                     colnr_T len, int has_props, int copy);
int buf_delete_line(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum, int flags);
```

The spelling and exact signatures should be settled in the first
implementation patch. The important properties are:

1. Every operation receives the target buffer explicitly.
2. The interface owns bounds checking, loaded/unloaded behavior, cache
   invalidation, and forwarding to memline.
3. Callers do not need to know that the implementation uses a memfile,
   cached line, locked block, or `memline_T`.
4. Read-only and writable access are visibly different. Prefer separate
   functions if that makes accidental mutation harder.
5. Pointer lifetime and whether a returned line includes text properties are
   documented at the interface boundary.

During the transition, current `ml_*` functions can remain as compatibility
wrappers. New code should not add direct `b_ml` access.

## Migration plan

### Phase 0: establish rules and inventory

- Keep this document as the migration checklist.
- Establish the rule: new code must use the buffer interface for line
  content, line count, loaded state, and empty-buffer checks. Direct `b_ml`
  access is permitted only inside the memline implementation until Phase 3.
- Generate a categorized inventory with searches for:
  - `->b_ml` and `curbuf->b_ml`;
  - `ml_get`, `ml_get_buf`, `ml_get_len`, and related accessors;
  - `ml_append`, `ml_replace`, `ml_delete`, and related mutation calls;
  - direct uses of `ml_line_ptr`, `ml_locked`, and memline flags.
- Classify each use as read, mutation, cache/state management, recovery/swap
  implementation, or test/support code. Do not mechanically replace the
  memline implementation itself.
- Run `python3 tools/check_internal_access.py`. Its report is grouped by source
  file in `internal_access.txt`, includes per-file statistics, and ends with
  totals. Treat its mutation section as a review inventory: it heuristically
  identifies line variables obtained from `ml_get*()` and subsequently written;
  verify each candidate against C control flow before changing it.
- Review `ml_get_buf(..., TRUE)` occurrences separately, since they grant
  writable cached-line access even when the returned pointer is not locally
  captured.

- Make `memline_T` private to the memline implementation if the include/layout

  provides `--all` for auditing the remaining legacy accesses.  The only
  implementation exception is `src/memline.c`.
- [ ] Re-run the inventory and require zero unclassified consumer accesses.

### Phase 4: harden and optimize

- Run the full test suite and feature-matrix builds, including minimal builds
  and language interfaces where available.
- Compare performance of hot paths such as screen drawing, insert/delete,
  syntax, and writing files. Avoid introducing allocations or buffer switches
  merely to obtain a line.
- Consider a future opaque buffer representation only after the accessor
  boundary is complete and measurable.

## Main challenges and decisions

### 1. `buf_T` is not currently opaque

The structure is defined in `src/structs.h` and many subsystems use fields
other than text. Hiding only `b_ml` may require include-order changes and
accessors for related state. Hiding the entire structure is a larger project;
do not couple it to the first line-access migration.

### 2. Implicit `curbuf` is deeply embedded

The existing mutation and convenience APIs often operate on `curbuf`. A
wrapper that silently switches buffers would be fragile: switching can run
autocommands, change windows, invalidate pointers, and alter error context.
The target API must carry `buf_T *` explicitly through the call chain.

### 3. Cached line pointer lifetime

A line pointer is valid only until a subsequent line access can flush or replace
the cache. The interface must preserve this contract or introduce an explicit
copy/borrow type. Do not “improve” lifetime accidentally by allocating every
line; that would affect hot paths and ownership assumptions.

### 4. Writable access and mutation bookkeeping

`ml_get_buf(..., TRUE)` marks cached state for modification, while
`ml_replace()` and friends handle undo, text properties, NetBeans, changed
state, and display updates through surrounding code. Reads and writes need
separate review and tests; a generic `line()` accessor must not make writes
look like harmless reads.

### 5. Unloaded, empty, invalid, and special buffers

A buffer can be never loaded, unloaded, empty, quickfix, terminal, prompt, or
otherwise special. Existing APIs return an empty string, an error marker, or
emit an error depending on the operation. The new interface must specify each
case and preserve the existing result and diagnostics.

### 6. Swap files, recovery, and memline cache state

`memline.c` manages block locking, translation, flushing, encryption, and
recovery. Direct field users may be coupled to these details in subtle ways.
Keep implementation-only operations in memline until their callers have a
well-defined replacement; do not replace state checks with a simplistic
“line count > 0” test.

### 7. Pointer invalidation across callbacks

Autocommands, scripting callbacks, redraw, and NetBeans can run while work is
in progress and may delete or unload a buffer. Existing `bufref_T` patterns
must remain in place. Accessors should not retain raw pointers across calls
that can invoke callbacks without revalidating the buffer.

### 8. Portability and generated declarations

Vim supports old and diverse C compilers. Keep signatures compatible with the
project's C dialect and use Vim types/wrappers. Changes to source functions
may require generated prototype updates; do not hand-edit generated files
unless the repository's normal generation step requires it.

### 9. Performance-sensitive call sites

Screen rendering, cursor movement, insert mode, syntax, and file writing can
access lines in tight loops. Thin inline wrappers may be appropriate after
correctness is established, but first measure rather than expose internals for
speed.

## Validation and completion criteria

A phase is complete only when:

- the relevant build succeeds without new warnings;
- focused buffer, editing, undo, recovery, swap-file, display, and scripting
  tests pass;
- behavior for unloaded and special buffers is covered;
- no newly migrated caller relies on a stale line pointer;
- the inventory is updated and the remaining direct accesses are explicitly
  justified as memline implementation code; and
- the full migration has a reviewable diff, not a broad formatting rewrite.

The overall upgrade is complete when external buffer consumers no longer read
`b_ml` or call implicit-current-buffer line operations, and the memline layout
can be changed without changing those consumers' code.

## Suggested patch sequence

1. Define the accessor contract and add read-only explicit-buffer wrappers.
2. Migrate line reads in one subsystem at a time, starting with low-risk
   consumers and including regression tests.
3. Migrate line count, loaded, and empty checks.
4. Add and migrate explicit-buffer mutation APIs.
5. Migrate integrations and macros; audit callback and `bufref_T` lifetimes.
6. Restrict direct memline access to implementation code and add enforcement.
7. Run full validation and measure hot paths before considering further
   encapsulation.

    colnr_T
ml_get_buf_len(buf_T *buf, linenr_T lnum)
{
    char_u	*line;

    if (*(line = ml_get_buf(buf, lnum, FALSE)) == NUL)
	return 0;

    if (buf->b_ml.ml_line_textlen <= 0)
	buf->b_ml.ml_line_textlen = (int)STRLEN(line) + 1;
    return buf->b_ml.ml_line_textlen - 1;
}
